statements.manuscript_statement_tex:
\label{lem:interval-cover}
Suppose that
\[
0<\min_{[0,1]^2}G_b
\leq\max_{[0,1]^2}G_b
<\min_{[0,1]^2}G_a,
\qquad
\max_{[0,1]^2}G_a<3\min_{[0,1]^2}G_b.
\]
Then every square \(Q\) described above satisfies
\[
G\bigl((u+3^{-n}C)\times(v+3^{-n}C)\bigr)
=[G(u,v),G(u+3^{-n},v+3^{-n})].
\]

lean_declarations.name: LambdaCantor.Classical.general_cantor_image
lean_declarations.lean_statement_text:
theorem general_cantor_image (function : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (continuous : ContinuousOn (fun point : ℝ × ℝ => function point.1 point.2)
      (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))
    (horizontalLower horizontalUpper verticalLower verticalUpper : ℝ)
    (bounds : CoordinateBounds function horizontalLower horizontalUpper verticalLower verticalUpper)
    (horizontal_nonnegative : 0 ≤ horizontalLower) (vertical_nonnegative : 0 ≤ verticalLower)
    (first_gap : verticalUpper ≤ horizontalLower)
    (middle_gap : horizontalUpper ≤ 3*verticalLower)
    (u v side : ℝ) (u_nonnegative : 0 ≤ u) (v_nonnegative : 0 ≤ v)
    (side_nonnegative : 0 ≤ side) (u_upper : u+side ≤ 1) (v_upper : v+side ≤ 1) :
    (fun point : ℝ × ℝ => function (u+side*point.1) (v+side*point.2)) ''
      (_root_.cantorSet ×ˢ _root_.cantorSet) =
        Set.Icc (function u v) (function (u+side) (v+side))

lean_declarations.name: LambdaCantor.Classical.coordinateBounds_of_partial_derivatives
lean_declarations.lean_statement_text:
theorem coordinateBounds_of_partial_derivatives
    (function : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (horizontalLower horizontalUpper verticalLower verticalUpper : ℝ)
    (horizontal_continuous : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      ContinuousOn (fun x => function x y) (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))
    (vertical_continuous : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      ContinuousOn (fun y => function x y) (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))
    (horizontal_differentiable : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      DifferentiableOn ℝ (fun x => function x y) (Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1))
    (vertical_differentiable : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      DifferentiableOn ℝ (fun y => function x y) (Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1))
    (horizontal_bounds : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1,
      horizontalLower ≤ deriv (fun t => function t y) x ∧
        deriv (fun t => function t y) x ≤ horizontalUpper)
    (vertical_bounds : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ y ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1,
      verticalLower ≤ deriv (fun t => function x t) y ∧
        deriv (fun t => function x t) y ≤ verticalUpper) :
    CoordinateBounds function horizontalLower horizontalUpper verticalLower verticalUpper

The derivative-to-increment theorem supplies CoordinateBounds from the displayed derivative extrema; its non-strict gap hypotheses are weaker than the strict manuscript assumptions.

statements.manuscript_statement_tex:
\label{ex:first-subdivision}
For a child with first ternary digits \(d,e\in\{0,2\}\) in the
\(a,b\) coordinates, write
\(a=(d+s)/3\), \(b=(e+t)/3\), with \(s,t\in[0,1]\).
Multiplying \(F(a,b)-3^{16}\) by \(9\) gives
\[
(19008+d+s)^2+9(1698+e+t)^2-3^{18}.
\]
Its corner-value intervals are
\[
\begin{array}{c@{\qquad}r@{\ ,\ }l}
\toprule
(d,e)&\multicolumn{2}{c}{\text{corner-value interval}}\\
\midrule
(0,0)&[-167589&-98999]\\
(0,2)&[-106425&-37799]\\
(2,0)&[-91553&-22959]\\
(2,2)&[-30389&38241]\\
\bottomrule
\end{array}
\]
Only the child \((2,2)\) meets the level zero.
Lemma~\ref{lem:interval-cover} makes this a statement about actual
Cantor points, not merely ordinary-square crossings.
The theorem proves that the surviving compact intersection is
perfect despite this first subdivision having a single surviving
child.

statements.manuscript_statement_tex:
\label{lem:strict-returns}
Let \(0<\lambda<1/2\), let \(L(s,t)\) be a positive linear function,
and let \(B\) be a compact
set of levels such that every \(u\in B\) has two incomparable
nonempty Cantor words returning its normalized level into
\(\operatorname{int}B\).
Then every sufficiently small Lipschitz perturbation of \(L\),
at every level sufficiently close to \(B\), has a positive-dimensional
zero set in \(C_\lambda^2\).

lean_declarations.name: LambdaCantor.Last.strict_return_criterion
lean_declarations.lean_statement_text:
theorem strict_return_criterion (ratio : ℝ) (hpositive : 0 < ratio) (hless : ratio < 1 / 2)
    (linear : (ℝ × ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (levels : Set ℝ)
    (hcompact : IsCompact levels) (hnonempty : levels.Nonempty)
    (hreturns : ∀ level ∈ levels, ∃ pair : ReturnPair,
      linearWordReturn ratio linear.toLinearMap (pair.word false) level ∈ interior levels ∧
      linearWordReturn ratio linear.toLinearMap (pair.word true) level ∈ interior levels) :
    ∃ threshold : ℝ, 0 < threshold ∧ ∃ neighborhood : Set ℝ,
      IsOpen neighborhood ∧ levels ⊆ neighborhood ∧
      ∀ bound : ℝ≥0, (bound : ℝ) < threshold →
      ∀ error : (ℝ × ℝ) → ℝ, LipschitzOnWith bound error (cantorDust ratio) → error 0 = 0 →
      ∀ level ∈ neighborhood,
        0 < dimH {point : ℝ × ℝ | point ∈ cantorDust ratio ∧ linear point + error point = level}

statements.scope_note: The perturbation error is normalized to vanish at the origin, absorbing its constant value into the target level. Returning words are nonempty and incomparable through ReturnPair. The theorem gives one threshold and an open neighborhood of the full compact level set.
statements.acceptance: source mapping only; final entry and current dependency closure require actual compilation

statements.manuscript_statement_tex:
\label{lem:irrational-tangent}
Suppose a \(C^1\) level curve in a Cantor rectangle contains a
nonempty compact perfect subset of \(C^2\).
If at one of its points the positive normalized derivative ratio
is irrational and lies in an admissible slope interval, then
the Cantor intersection of the curve has positive Hausdorff dimension.

lean_declarations.name: LambdaCantor.Integer.good_slope_positive_dimension_of_perfect_subset
lean_declarations.lean_statement_text:
theorem good_slope_positive_dimension_of_perfect_subset
    (function : (ℝ × ℝ) → ℝ) (level horizontal vertical : ℝ)
    (vertical_positive : 0 < vertical)
    (good : GoodSlope (horizontal/vertical))
    (irrational : ∀ rational : ℚ, horizontal/vertical ≠ (rational : ℝ))
    (source : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) (perfect : Perfect source)
    (contained : source ⊆ {point : ℝ × ℝ | point ∈ cantorDust (1/3) ∧ function point = level})
    (point : ℝ × ℝ) (membership : point ∈ source)
    (smooth : ContDiffAt ℝ 1 function point)
    (derivative : (ℝ × ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (differentiable : HasFDerivAt function derivative point)
    (formula : ∀ direction, derivative direction = horizontal*direction.1+vertical*direction.2) :
    0 < dimH {point : ℝ × ℝ | point ∈ cantorDust (1/3) ∧ function point = level}

statements.scope_note: The endpoint requires only a perfect subset through the selected point; compactness of that subset is unnecessary. The local C1 hypothesis supplies the actual strict derivative, and the full Cantor level need not itself be perfect.

statements.manuscript_statement_tex:
\label{lem:root-fibres}
Fix \(\alpha>1\), two cylinder coordinates \(x_\omega(\lambda)\),
\(y_\tau(\lambda)\) of lengths \(h,\ell\), and
\([a,b]\subset(1/4,1/2)\) on which both coordinates stay positive.
Suppose every paired address has a unique root of
\(x_\omega(\lambda)^\alpha+y_\tau(\lambda)^\alpha=1\) in \([a,b]\),
and the parameter derivative of the residual is bounded away
from zero at all these roots.
The distribution of these roots under fair independent addresses
is absolutely continuous, and for almost every parameter with
respect to that distribution,
\[
\dim_{\mathrm H}(E_{\alpha,\lambda})=\frac{\log4}{\log(1/\lambda)}-1.
\]

lean_declarations.name: LambdaCantor.First.Roots.root_fibres
lean_declarations.lean_statement_text: theorem root_fibres {exponent : ℝ} (data : RootFibreData exponent) : RootFibreConclusion data

lean_declarations.name: LambdaCantor.First.Roots.RootFibreData
lean_declarations.lean_statement_text:
structure RootFibreData (exponent : ℝ) where
  exponent_gt_one : 1 < exponent
  lower : ℝ
  upper : ℝ
  lower_gt_quarter : 1 / 4 < lower
  upper_lt_half : upper < 1 / 2
  ordered : lower ≤ upper
  leftWord : ℕ → Bool
  rightWord : ℕ → Bool

  rightLength : ℕ

statements.manuscript_statement_tex:
\label{lem:two-bands}
Let \(0<\lambda<1/2\), and let \(f,g\) be increasing \(C^1\)
functions on \([0,1]\) with positive derivatives.
If all ratios \(g'(t)/f'(s)\), \(s,t\in[0,1]\), are greater than
one and belong to a compact subinterval of either
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-bands}
\left(\frac1\lambda-1-\lambda,\frac1{1-\lambda}\right)
\quad\text{or}\quad
\left(\frac1\lambda-1,\frac1{1-\lambda-\lambda^2}\right),
\end{equation}
then every strict interior level of \(f+g\) on \([0,1]^2\)
meets \(C_\lambda^2\) in a set of positive Hausdorff dimension.

lean_declarations.name: LambdaCantor.Last.two_band_separable_c1_closed_interval_criterion
lean_declarations.lean_statement_text:
theorem two_band_separable_c1_closed_interval_criterion
    {first second : ℝ → ℝ} {ratio level lower upper : ℝ}
    (hfirst : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 first (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))
    (hsecond : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 second (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1))
    (hpositive : 0 < ratio) (hhalf : ratio < 1 / 2)
    (hfirst_positive : ∀ coordinate ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      0 < derivWithin first (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) coordinate)
    (hsecond_positive : ∀ coordinate ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      0 < derivWithin second (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) coordinate)
    (bands : TwoBandInterval ratio lower upper)
    (hratios : ∀ firstCoordinate ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      ∀ secondCoordinate ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
        lower ≤ derivWithin second (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) secondCoordinate /
          derivWithin first (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) firstCoordinate ∧
        derivWithin second (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) secondCoordinate /
          derivWithin first (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) firstCoordinate ≤ upper)
    (hlevel : level ∈ Set.Ioo (first 0 + second 0) (first 1 + second 1)) :
    0 < dimH {point : ℝ × ℝ | point ∈ cantorDust ratio ∧
      first point.1 + second point.2 = level}

\label{lem:average-sobolev}
Let \([a,b]\subset(3/8,1/2)\) be sufficiently short that
\[
0<2\sigma<\frac{2\log(8/3)}{\log(b/a^3)}-1.
\]
On every compact subinterval of \((a,b)\), the squared
\(H^\sigma\) norm of \(\mu_\lambda*\mu_\lambda\) is integrable
with respect to \(\lambda\).

theorem average_sobolev {lower upper regularity : ℝ}
    (lower_above_three_eighths : 3/8 < lower) (ordered : lower ≤ upper)
    (upper_below_half : upper < 1/2) (regularity_positive : 0 < regularity)
    (regularity_range : 2*regularity <
      2*Real.log (8/3 : ℝ)/Real.log (upper/lower^3)-1) :
    (∀ compact : Set ℝ, compact ⊆ Set.Ioo lower upper → IsCompact compact →
      (∫⁻ ratio in compact, AE.canonicalSobolevEnergy ratio regularity) < ⊤ ∧
      IntegrableOn (fun ratio => (AE.canonicalSobolevEnergy ratio regularity).toReal) compact volume) ∧
    (∀ᵐ ratio : ℝ, ratio ∈ Set.Ioo lower upper →
      AE.HasCanonicalSobolevDensity (AE.selfConvolutionProbability ratio) regularity)

def HasSobolevDensity (probability : Measure ℝ) (regularity : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ density : ℝ → ℝ, Integrable density volume ∧ MemLp density 2 volume ∧

    probability = volume.withDensity (fun value => ENNReal.ofReal (density value)) ∧
    (∫⁻ frequency : ℝ, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + |frequency| ^ (2 * regularity)) *
      ‖𝓕 (fun value => (density value : ℂ)) frequency‖ ^ 2)) < ⊤
